Differential testing

How Offing's findings compare with Renovate, xeol, and Pluto, and what each disagreement means. The summary and the accuracy table are on Validation.

Differential testing against Renovate

Renovate is the closest widely used tool, so the report compares Offing's findings with Renovate's for the same repository, by rule family. A maintainer runs Renovate (it needs the network and a large download; it is not part of npm run check or any scan). Give it a read-only GitHub token, or it cannot look up GitHub Actions:

export RENOVATE_TOKEN=<token> GITHUB_COM_TOKEN=<token>
npx renovate --platform=local --dry-run=lookup --report-type=file --report-path=renovate.json
npm run differential:renovate -- --renovate renovate.json --repository . --name owner/repo --out report.json

The two tools answer different questions. Renovate says a newer version exists and prints npm deprecation notices; it has no end-of-life data. Offing says a release line is past its vendor's end of life; it does not say an update exists. So the report only compares where both can speak about one dependency in one file:

Family Offing Renovate Counted as agreement
deprecated-package npm.package.* findings npm deprecationMessage both mark the package deprecated
base-image container.* findings dockerfile / docker-compose updates Renovate offers an update for the image Offing calls end-of-life
github-action github-actions.* findings github-actions updates Renovate offers an update for the action Offing flags

Outcomes: agree, offing-only, renovate-only, and inconclusive (Renovate skipped the lookup, for example github-token-required for Actions when run without a GitHub token, so it says nothing either way). Runtime findings (nodejs.runtime.*, python.runtime.*) have no Renovate counterpart and are listed as not comparable. Matching is by file and dependency name because Renovate gives no line numbers.

The committed reports are combined into one reviewable page, differential-report.md (and differential-report.json), which lists every disagreement with links to the declaration at the pinned commit and to each tool's evidence. Regenerate it with npm run differential:report after adding or refreshing a report; a test fails when it drifts from the reports.

Results for the five container corpus repositories, with Renovate 44.164 run with a read-only GitHub token on 2026-10-23 (reports in benchmarks/differential/reports/, trimmed Renovate output in tests/fixtures/differential/):

Repository Agree Offing-only Renovate-only Inconclusive
outline/outline 22 5 13 0
excalidraw/excalidraw 23 2 2 0
mealie-recipes/mealie 17 0 4 0
umami-software/umami 8 1 0 0
gethomepage/homepage 0 0 0 0

What it shows:

  • Agreements are 10 base images, 53 GitHub Action findings, and 7 npm deprecations. Where Offing calls node or postgres end-of-life, or flags actions/checkout on Node 20, Renovate offers a newer major version. Renovate does not say the old line is unsupported; only Offing does.
  • No comparison is inconclusive. With a token Renovate looks up every GitHub Action, so the Action findings that were inconclusive in the 2026-10-16 run are now comparisons, and all of them agree.
  • Renovate-only are npm deprecations Offing has no rule for (for example @types/diff, @types/glob, @nuxt/types, react-waypoint). This is the real gap: the npm-deprecated importer only checks a candidate list, so these names are candidates to add. Each is a Renovate observation, not evidence; the importer still requires the registry's own deprecation notice.
  • Offing-only is not a real disagreement yet. All eight entries are packages Renovate does list, under a different spelling: the comparison reads the package name from the rule id, so @types/dotenv becomes types.dotenv and next with a version-line rule becomes next.14. Six of the Renovate-only @types/* entries are the same packages seen from the other side. Matching by the rule's package name is a follow-up to this comparison.

Differential testing against xeol

xeol reports release cycles of products (runtimes, databases, npm packages) that endoflife.date lists as past end of life, for versions it finds in lockfiles and image filesystems. A maintainer runs it (it downloads an EOL database; it is not part of npm run check or any scan):

xeol dir:<checkout> -o json > xeol.json
npm run differential:xeol -- --xeol xeol.json --repository <checkout> --name owner/repo --out report.json

The report compares by product, not by file: xeol names the lockfile that resolved a version, Offing names the manifest that declares it. Offing runtime, container image, and npm package findings are compared with the xeol product of the same name (node images with nodejs, golang with go, postgres with postgresql). Outcomes: agree (both report the product), offing-only, and xeol-only. GitHub Actions, CI images, and the other families xeol has no product for are listed as not comparable.

Results for the five repositories of the Renovate comparison, with xeol 0.10.8 run with dir: on the pinned checkouts on 2026-10-23 (reports in benchmarks/differential/reports/xeol/, trimmed xeol output in tests/fixtures/xeol/):

Repository Agree Offing-only xeol-only
excalidraw/excalidraw 0 3 0
gethomepage/homepage 0 0 0
mealie-recipes/mealie 0 2 2
outline/outline 0 11 0
umami-software/umami 1 4 1

What the numbers say:

  • Agreement is rare because the tools read different files. xeol dir: resolves versions from lockfiles; it does not read Dockerfiles, workflow files, .nvmrc, or engines. Every Offing runtime and image finding here is therefore Offing-only, and not a sign that xeol disagrees. Where both read the same dependency, they agree: both call next 13 end of life in umami.
  • xeol-only are npm packages whose release line endoflife.date lists as ended (vue 2.6 and 3.2, vuetify 2). Offing has no rule for them; each is a candidate for the npm-support-end importer, not evidence by itself.
  • Not compared: GitHub Actions findings, which are the largest Offing family in these repositories and which xeol does not model.

Differential testing against Pluto

Pluto reads apiVersion and kind from manifests and says whether the Kubernetes project still serves them, which is the question the kubernetes detector answers. A maintainer runs it (it is not part of npm run check or any scan). Run it from inside the checkout, because Pluto joins --directory to the working directory:

(cd <checkout> && pluto detect-files -d . -o json -t k8s=v1.36.0 > pluto.json)
npm run differential:pluto -- --pluto pluto.json --repository <checkout> --name owner/repo --out report.json

Findings are compared by file, kind, API group, and version. Outcomes: agree (Pluto reports the version as removed at the target version), offing-only, pluto-only, and pluto-deprecated-only (deprecated but still served; Offing judges only removed versions, so this is not a disagreement). Non-Kubernetes findings are listed as not comparable.

Results for the seventeen Kubernetes corpus repositories, with Pluto 5.24.4 at target k8s=v1.36.0 on the pinned checkouts on 2026-10-23 (reports in benchmarks/differential/reports/pluto/, trimmed Pluto output in tests/fixtures/pluto/; repositories with no Kubernetes finding from either tool are left out of the table):

Repository Agree Offing-only Pluto-only Pluto deprecated-only
FairwindsOps/pluto 1 1 3 0
doitintl/kube-no-trouble 0 0 38 1
hasura/skor 0 0 1 0
kelseyhightower/ingress-with-static-ip 1 0 0 0
kelseyhightower/kubernetes-cluster-federation 5 0 0 0
knrt10/kubernetes-basicLearning 1 0 0 0
kubernetes/examples 10 0 0 0
luksa/kubernetes-in-action 27 0 0 0
lusyoe/springboot-k8s-example 1 1 0 0
motiv-labs/janus 0 2 0 0
ossf/package-analysis 1 0 0 0
unixhot/salt-kubebin 15 0 0 0
Total 62 4 42 1

Every difference has one of three causes, none of them a wrong finding:

  • Offing-only are Helm templates (charts/templates/ingress.yaml, janus/templates/*.yaml, a test chart). Pluto cannot parse files with template actions and skips them; Offing reads the apiVersion and kind lines of a template. This is Offing finding more.
  • Pluto-only are kind: List items (hasura/skor, one Pluto test asset), JSON manifests, and files under fixtures/ and testdata/ directories (doitintl/kube-no-trouble has 38, FairwindsOps/pluto three). The detector page lists these as not judged. Pluto finding more here is the known cost of Offing's conservative scope, and the same forms are why the blind repositories were rechecked by hand.
  • Disagreement on a version Offing does judge is zero: all 62 manifests that both tools read agree on removed.
